candidate.blueprint_topic: Management of Care — professional performance monitoring and privileging
candidate.educational_objective: Explain that OPPE provides ongoing qualitative and quantitative performance data used to detect trends, guide privileging decisions, and identify when focused evaluation may be necessary.

options.A: To replace credentialing and privileging with payroll and scheduling data once the practitioner begins working.
options.B: To repeat the initial focused professional practice evaluation continuously for every practitioner regardless of performance.
options.C: To collect performance data for archival purposes only, without using the information in decisions about existing privileges.
options.D: To identify professional-practice trends and use current performance data to support decisions about continuing, limiting, or revoking privileges and whether focused evaluation is needed.

candidate.rationale: The Joint Commission states that OPPE identifies professional-practice trends that may affect quality and safety and creates an objective, data-driven basis for re-privileging decisions. OPPE data are used to determine whether existing privileges should continue, be limited or revoked, and whether a performance concern requires focused professional practice evaluation. Therefore D is correct. A is unrelated to OPPE. B incorrectly treats FPPE as a continuous universal process. C contradicts the requirement that OPPE data be used in decision-making.
candidate.source_claim_supported: OPPE is an ongoing data-driven process used to identify professional-practice trends that may affect quality and safety and to inform privileging decisions, including whether focused evaluation or other action is required.
